text:
maya: @cta-arch / @arch-team wave — PR #10002 is blocked on a short design note or RFC pointer before we can merge. This is a small routing shim to route heavy/long requests to the dedicated pool. Impact: ~+30ms p50 on default path, reduces p95 tail for heavy requests. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pr/10002 :wave:

jon: ping — I own the PR, added unit tests and an e2e smoke job. main open bit is the arch stamp + a short compatibility note.

maya: quick summary + proposed canary plan below. asking for either an RFC link or a 1-paragraph decision note to attach to the PR so release/corp-compliance can sign off. :mag:

maya: Proposed canary (suggested):
```
- Canary window: 02:00-04:00 UTC
- Ramp: 0% -> 5% (30m) -> 25% (60m) -> 100% (final)
- Monitoring: p50/p95 latency, error rate, rejection-rate, quota-throttles
- Fallback: automated toggle to previous routing policy + drain routing nodes
```

cta-arch: quick read — looks small, but please add a compatibility matrix (how old clients behave) and a short risks section. specifically: how does the shim affect KV cache keys and TTL? if you add that I'll do a brief review and can potentially +1.

jon: rough config diff (excerpt) is in the PR, e.g.:
```yaml
routing_policy: 
  name: heavy-path-shim
  enabled: false
  threshold_tokens: 2048
  fallback_timeout_ms: 500
```

maya: added compatibility bullets and a risk note to the PR: - clients < 2.1 get routed to default pool; - fallback maintains previous behavior; - risk: potential cache fragmentation if routing changes key composition. RFC stub: https://rfc.internal/infra-routing-shim (private). PTAL @cta-arch. :rocket:

cta-arch: ok saw the updates. still worried about cache key entropy and TTL interactions — could cause higher cold miss rate for some workloads. please call that out in the risk section and add a backoff for cold cache cases. once that's in i'll do a fast +1 and recommend 2hr canary.

sam: quick ops question — will infra need to pre-warm dedicated nodes before canary starts? cc @eng-infra.

maya: yeah we'll add a pre-warm step to the rollout playbook. deploy-bot: canaries prefer 02:00-05:00 UTC window on infra calendar.

deploy-bot: Scheduling note — canary proposed for 2026-05-12 02:00-05:00 UTC (placeholder). Please confirm finalize 24h before.

maya: thanks — i'll update PR with cache-note, backoff, and pre-warm steps. bumping proposed canary to 2hr per @cta-arch. pinging back when updated.

cta-arch: :thumbsup: i'll re-review after the cache note addition and reply with final blessing or minor comments.

jon: thanks all — aiming to update PR in the next 90m and request final review.
